summary: Import-time exec of base64-decoded payload (Windows MessageBox)
details: On import, shark_e2e_test/__init__.py decodes a base64 blob and passes it to exec() unconditionally. The decoded payload is a Windows-only ctypes call that displays a MessageBoxW with the literal strings 'shark'/'Shark'. The current payload performs no network I/O, no filesystem reads, no credential access, and establishes no persistence — its only effect is a GUI popup on Windows. However, the mechanism (top-level obfuscated exec of a base64 blob on import) is the canonical dropper scaffold: the same code path would execute arbitrary attacker logic if the blob were swapped, and the obfuscation prevents transparent review of intent. The package name and limited utility (a popup with the literal string 'shark') are also consistent with a test/PoC artifact rather than a legitimate library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
